title: Class 1 · Cambridge 18 Test 1
summary: In class: Listening Part 2 (Becoming a volunteer for ACE) and Reading Passage 1 (Urban farming). Redo both here with the real audio and the real exam pages, then learn the words and paraphrase pairs that came out of the lesson.

listening.title: Becoming a volunteer for ACE
listening.scenario: Talk to a group of new volunteers
listening.instructions: Questions 11–13: choose A, B or C. Questions 14 and 15: choose TWO letters. Questions 16–20: match each area of voluntary work with one letter A–G. 10 marks.

questions.q: Why does the speaker apologise about the seats?
options: They are too small.
There are not enough of them.
Some of them are very close together.
questions.explanation: The speaker says extra seats were brought in so nobody has to stand, but some people may be 'a bit squashed' — squashed = very close together.
questions.tip: The answer usually comes after the contrast word 'but'. Hearing 'extra seats' and picking B is the trap: extra seats is the opposite of 'not enough'.

questions.q: What does the speaker say about the age of volunteers?
options: The age of volunteers is less important than other factors.
Young volunteers are less reliable than older ones.
Most volunteers are about 60 years old.
questions.explanation: Volunteers can be as young as 16 or 60 and over, and age is not related to reliability — so age matters less than other things.
questions.tip: When an option contains a comparative (less reliable), check that the recording actually compares the two groups. Here it denies the comparison.

questions.q: What does the speaker say about training?
options: It is continuous.
It is conducted by a manager.
It takes place online.
questions.explanation: Training happens before, during and after periods of work — that is 'continuous'. It is run by experienced volunteers, not managers, and it is face-to-face, not online.
questions.tip: 'before, during and after' is the paraphrase of continuous. Two distractors are directly contradicted, so eliminate as you listen.

questions.q: Which TWO issues does the speaker ask the audience to consider before they apply to be volunteers?
options: their financial situation
their level of commitment
their work experience
their ambition
their availability
questions.explanation: 'What we value is dedication' = level of commitment; 'it is critical that you have enough hours' = availability. Income is explicitly ruled out ('we don't ask about income'), and work experience and ambition are never mentioned.
questions.tip: For TWO-letter questions, tick each letter the moment you hear it. Do not wait until the end and try to remember.

questions.q: Fundraising

bank.t: an understanding of food and diet

questions.explanation: The speaker asks for an imaginative or novel way of raising money. novel ≈ original, new.

questions.q: Litter collection

bank.t: an understanding of food and diet

questions.explanation: Volunteers walk for long periods, sometimes uphill — that describes physical fitness, not a skill.

questions.q: 'Playmates'

bank.t: an understanding of food and diet

questions.explanation: Helpers need to know something about nutrition. nutrition ≈ food and diet. 'Working with children' tempts you towards C, but parenting skills are never asked for.

questions.q: Story club

bank.t: an understanding of food and diet

questions.explanation: Reading stories to an audience is described as acting — acting ≈ experience on stage.

questions.q: First aid

bank.t: an understanding of food and diet

questions.explanation: You must not forget any important step of the procedure — that is a good memory.

notes.d: but / however / actually / in fact — the information after them is what the question is testing. Mark them while you listen.

notes.t: Distractors repeat the words you expect
notes.d: Options often reuse a word you have just heard (extra seats, 60 years old, manager). Match the meaning, not the word.
The box (A–G) never uses the words you hear. novel→original ideas, uphill walking→fitness, nutrition→food and diet, steps of a procedure→memory.

listening.title: Talk on jobs in fashion design
listening.scenario: Two students discuss a careers talk
listening.instructions: Homework set in class: do this blind — no script, one listen. Questions 21–26 choose A, B or C; 27 & 28 and 29 & 30 choose TWO letters. 10 marks.

questions.q: What problem did Chantal have at the start of the talk?
options: Her view of the speaker was blocked.
She was unable to find an empty seat.
The students next to her were talking.

questions.q: What were Hugo and Chantal surprised to hear about the job market?
options: It has become more competitive than it used to be.
There is more variety in it than they had realised.
Some areas of it are more exciting than others.

questions.q: Hugo and Chantal agree that the speaker's message was
options: unfair to them at times.
hard for them to follow.
critical of the industry.

questions.q: What do Hugo and Chantal criticise about their school careers advice?
options: when they received the advice
how much advice was given
who gave the advice

questions.q: When discussing their future, Hugo and Chantal disagree on
options: which is the best career in fashion.
when to choose a career in fashion.
why they would like a career in fashion.

questions.q: How does Hugo feel about being an unpaid assistant?
options: He is realistic about the practice.
He feels the practice is dishonest.
He thinks others want to change the practice.

questions.q: Which TWO mistakes did the speaker admit she made in her first job?
options: being dishonest to her employer
paying too much attention to how she looked
expecting to become well known
trying to earn a lot of money
openly disliking her client

questions.q: Which TWO pieces of retail information do Hugo and Chantal agree would be useful?
options: the reasons people return fashion items
how much time people have to shop for clothes
fashion designs people want but can't find
the best time of year for fashion buying
the most popular fashion sizes

notes.d: 1) One blind listen, answer as you go. 2) Mark every question you guessed. 3) Only then open the script, underline every contrast marker, and write down the paraphrase that caught you out.
Most questions test who thinks what and whether the two speakers agree. Track agreement words: 'exactly', 'true, but', 'I'm not so sure'.

reading.title: Urban farming
reading.instructions: Questions 1–3: sentence completion, NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER. Questions 4–7: table, ONE WORD ONLY. Questions 8–13: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN. Target time 20 minutes.

questions.q: Vertical tubes are used to grow strawberries, ________ and herbs.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 lists what grows in the vertical tubes: strawberries, then rows of lettuces, then aromatic herbs.
questions.tip: Completion answers appear in passage order. Copy the exact word and keep the plural.

questions.q: There will eventually be a daily harvest of as much as ________ in weight of fruit and vegetables.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2: when the rest of the roof is in production, staff will harvest up to 1,000 kg a day.
questions.tip: 'NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER' lets you write the number plus the unit.

questions.q: It may be possible that the farm's produce will account for as much as 10% of the city's ________ overall.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 quotation: with enough unused space you could target between 5% and 10% of consumption.
questions.tip: This is the long sentence you broke down in class: 'there's no reason why you shouldn't…' — a double negative, so it means you can.

questions.q: Intensive farming · Growth: wide range of ________ used
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3: most of the fruit and vegetables we eat have been treated with around 17 different pesticides.
questions.tip: ONE WORD ONLY here, so 'different pesticides' would be marked wrong.

questions.q: Intensive farming · Selection: varieties of fruit and vegetables chosen that can survive long ________
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4: varieties are selected for their capacity to withstand substantial journeys.
questions.tip: withstand ≈ survive. The table paraphrases the passage, so match the idea, not the wording.

questions.q: Intensive farming · Sale: ________ receive very little of overall income
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4: 80% of the price goes to wholesalers and transport companies, not the producers.
questions.tip: 'not the producers' is the clue — the negative in the passage becomes 'very little' in the table.

questions.q: Aeroponic urban farming · Selection: produce chosen because of its ________
questions.explanation: Paragraph 5: you can select crop varieties for their flavour rather than their resistance to transport.
questions.tip: Both British and American spellings are accepted in the real exam.

questions.q: Urban farming can take place above or below ground.
questions.explanation: Rooftop farms are above ground and mushrooms are grown in underground car parks — both are stated.

questions.q: Some of the equipment used in aeroponic farming can be made by hand.
questions.explanation: The passage says the equipment is light, easy to install and cheap to buy, but never says who or how it is made.
questions.tip: NOT GIVEN is the default when the statement adds a new detail the passage simply does not discuss.

questions.q: Urban farming relies more on electricity than some other types of farming.
questions.explanation: The opposite is stated: it consumes a tiny fraction of the electricity used by some other techniques.

questions.q: Fruit and vegetables grown on an aeroponic urban farm are cheaper than traditionally grown organic produce.
questions.explanation: Prices are higher than classic intensive agriculture but lower than soil-based organic growers.

questions.q: Most produce can be grown on an aeroponic urban farm at any time of the year.
questions.explanation: Much of the produce is suited to the summer months, so not all year round.

questions.q: Beans take longer to grow on an urban farm than other vegetables.
questions.explanation: Beans are mentioned only for taking up a lot of space for little return. Growing time is never compared.

notes.t: Completion tasks follow the passage order
notes.d: Questions 1–7 run top to bottom through the passage. If you cannot find number 5, it sits between the places where 4 and 6 were found.
Take the word from the passage, do not rewrite it. Check the word limit, singular vs plural, numbers and units before you move on.
'there's no reason why you shouldn't…' — pattern: there is no reason why + clause, plus a double negative. Meaning: reaching 5–10% of what the city eats is entirely possible.
'…uses 90% less water than a classic intensive farm for the same yield.' Pattern: X% less + noun + than Y + for the same Z. Reuse it in Writing Task 1 and in environment essays.
Urban agriculture, food miles, greenhouse gas emissions and water use all belong to the environment topic. Store the passage's phrases as ready-made Task 2 sentences.

vocab.def_en: farming that uses a lot of chemicals and machinery to get the largest possible crop from the land
vocab.example: Intensive farming raises output, but it pollutes the air and exhausts the soil.

vocab.def_en: the amount that is produced; (verb) to give in to pressure
vocab.example: The same yield can be achieved with 90% less water.
vocab.synonyms: output, harvest; give in to, succumb to

vocab.def_en: the amount of something that people use, eat or drink
vocab.example: Rooftop farms could eventually cover a tenth of the city's food consumption.

vocab.def_en: a gas such as carbon dioxide that traps heat in the atmosphere
vocab.example: Shipping food thousands of kilometres generates huge quantities of greenhouse gases.

vocab.def_en: a chemical used to kill insects that damage crops
vocab.example: Much of the fruit we eat has been treated with more than a dozen pesticides.

vocab.def_en: something you can choose instead of something else
vocab.example: Soil-free growing is a credible alternative to conventional agriculture.

vocab.def_en: to change your behaviour so that you fit new conditions
vocab.example: Farmers must adapt to a hotter and drier growing season.

vocab.def_en: to stop resisting something and give in to it
vocab.example: Regulators should not succumb to pressure from the food industry.

vocab.def_en: something that limits what you are able to do
vocab.example: In cities you work with very significant practical constraints on space.

vocab.def_en: an occasion or place that displays the best qualities of something
vocab.example: The rooftop farm is a real-life showcase for soil-free growing.

vocab.def_en: to be strong enough not to be harmed by something
vocab.example: Varieties are chosen for their capacity to withstand long journeys.

vocab.def_en: to use something up completely
vocab.example: No soil is exhausted, because the roots grow in nutrient-rich water.

vocab.def_en: existing in very large quantities
vocab.example: Strawberries sprout abundantly from the vertical tubes.

vocab.def_en: the crop that is gathered in; to gather a crop
vocab.example: Twenty staff will harvest up to a tonne of produce every day.

vocab.def_en: fruit and vegetables that are grown to be sold
vocab.example: The farm's produce is grown upstairs and sold just down the road.

vocab.def_en: a business that buys goods in bulk and sells them on to shops
vocab.example: Most of the price goes to wholesalers rather than to the farmers.

vocab.def_en: to treat something so that it can be used again
vocab.example: The water that showers the roots every twelve minutes is recycled.

vocab.def_en: morally good; describing a system in which each part improves the others
vocab.example: He calls the method virtuous: cheap to run, clean and entirely local.

vocab.def_en: no longer in use
vocab.example: Mushrooms are being grown in disused underground car parks.

vocab.def_en: a very small part of something
vocab.example: The system uses a tiny fraction of the electricity older methods need.
vocab.synonyms: a small proportion of, a sliver of

vocab.def_en: willingness to give your time and energy to something
vocab.example: Think carefully about your level of commitment before you apply.

vocab.def_en: hard work and loyalty towards something you care about
vocab.example: What the charity values most in its volunteers is dedication.

vocab.def_en: how much free time you have to do something
vocab.example: It is critical that your availability matches the hours we need.

vocab.def_en: the quality of being someone others can depend on
vocab.example: Age has nothing to do with reliability.

vocab.def_en: new and different from anything done before
vocab.example: We are looking for a novel way of raising money.

vocab.def_en: full of new and interesting ideas
vocab.example: An imaginative fundraiser attracts far more donors than a familiar one.

vocab.def_en: pressed together in a space that is too small
vocab.example: People at the back may be a bit squashed, so do come forward.

vocab.def_en: the activity of collecting money for a charity or cause
vocab.example: Fundraising needs original ideas far more than it needs money.

synonyms.q: Some of them are very close together

synonyms.src: before, during and after periods of work
it is critical that you have enough hours
an imaginative or novel way of fundraising
walk for long periods, sometimes uphill

synonyms.q: an understanding of food and diet

synonyms.src: reading stories is a kind of acting
not forget any important steps or details

synonyms.q: producers receive very little of overall income
synonyms.src: 80% of the price goes to wholesalers and transport companies
select crop varieties for their flavour, not their resistance to transport
consuming a tiny fraction of the electricity used by some techniques

notes.t: Listening · the answer lives after the contrast
notes.d: but / however / actually / in fact. Everything before them is usually the distractor.
If an option says 'less reliable', 'more expensive', 'the most popular', the recording has to make that comparison. Very often it denies it.
Tick each letter as you hear it. Never wait to the end and reconstruct from memory.
Locate with the keyword you highlighted, copy the exact word, obey the word limit, check plurals, numbers and units.
FALSE = the passage says the opposite. NOT GIVEN = the passage never discusses it. Q9 and Q13 are NOT GIVEN, Q10 and Q12 are FALSE.
there is no reason why + clause (没有理由不…) and shouldn't + double negative = a positive claim.

homework: Listening Part 3: blind listen once, do Q21–30, no script.
Then read the Part 3 script and underline every contrast marker (but / however / although).
Write out the paraphrase pairs from Part 3 the way we did for Part 2.
Listen to Part 2 three times: once for answers, once with the script, once shadowing.
Reread Urban farming without the questions — intensive reading of the whole passage.
Collect every paraphrase and environment word from the passage into your notebook.
Break down the two long sentences from class into clauses.
Study the 28 words from this class in the flashcards.
